title: Client risk loci mindmap - negotiation notes
content:
Purpose: quick personal map of where risk concentrates for client contracts (prioritize redlines + negotiation scripts). Not formal — notes to self and rapid counters for AE / Deals.

Context: enterprise prospect pushing for broad indemnities, aggressive data retention terms, and unclear subprocessor language. They are also asking for very low latency SLA credits (we need to preserve scoped availability obligations and avoid punitive liquidated damages).

High-risk loci (at-a-glance):
- Indemnity scope: ask: unlimited for any third-party claims.
  - Watch for: 'all claims' language that picks up model outputs and downstream customer claims.
  - Target counter: carveout for claims arising from Customer-provided data, and for outputs that are user-provided prompts. Cap indemnity to direct damages caused by willful misconduct + exclude model-creative-output litigation unless provable data injection.

- Liability cap and formula: customer pushing to eliminate cap or tie to ARR.
  - Preferred: 1–3x fees (12 month lookback) with exceptions for gross negligence/willful misconduct.
  - Negotiation lever: offer higher cap with premium pricing / purchase of extended indemnity add-on.

- Data residency & export: they want strict in-region storage + right to full export on termination.
  - Watch: operational burden + compliance with shared logs.
  - Ask: commit to region residency for customer data (not model telemetry) and define export format, fee, and timeframe (30–60 days).

- Subprocessors & subprocessors notice: they want pre-approval of any subprocessor and flow-down of all obligations.
  - Counter: require notice + right to object for high-risk subprocessors, allow standard approved roster with security + SOC2 attestation.

- Security incident & breach notice: timeline and remediation obligations.
  - We can accept 72-hour notice for confirmed incidents; 24-hour for suspected PII exfiltration is too aggressive operationally.
  - Ask for cooperative remediation and joint notification language.

- Termination & transition assistance: they want long tail free transition.
  - Counter: standard 90 days paid transition assistance or reasonable support subject to fees; offer one complimentary export on termination.

- IP & outputs: who owns model outputs? they ask for right to use/transforms unrestricted.
  - Key: preserve model IP and pre-trained weights; grant customer a license to outputs for their app with normal use rights. Carve out underlying model weights, improvements, and telemetry.

Negotiation levers (script fragments):
- When they say 'we need unlimited liability' -> "We understand the concern; to cover that exposure we can increase the liability cap to X if you agree to specific data handling safeguards and a run-rate-based commercial commitment."
- For 'pre-approval of all subprocessors' -> "We operate on an approved-subprocessor roster; for any new high-risk subprocessor we will notify you and provide SOC2 / security docs so you can escalate if needed."
- For tight SLA credits -> "We can increase uptime targets for a premium and define credits as a portion of the monthly invoice, not punitive. Let's map latency-sensitive endpoints separately so we can offer objective SLOs."

Mitigations / trade instruments:
- Escrow / source access: limited to agreed triggers (bankruptcy/long stop failure), not general dev access.
- Insurance: require proof of tech E&O; propose customer take insured position if pushing unlimited exposure.
- Audit window: offer annual security review vs continuous deep audit.

Quick templates / handy clauses to paste:
- Data export: "Upon termination, we will provide Customer an extract of Customer Data in commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days upon written request; additional exports or ongoing transition support are billable."
- Subprocessor notice: "Provider shall maintain an up-to-date list of subprocessors and provide notice of any additions; Customer may object to a new subprocessor on reasonable security grounds within 15 days."
- Liability carveout: "Neither party's liability for indirect, special, incidental or consequential damages shall exceed the total fees paid in the prior 12 months, except in cases of gross negligence or willful misconduct."

Scenario sketches (decision tree shorthand):
- If customer insists on unlimited ip indemnity -> request meeting with legal + sales; propose alternative of limited cap + targeted warranty for specified IP classes.
- If data residency must be region-only -> ops to estimate infra cost; if >$X/month escalate to pricing.
- If they demand full pre-approval of subprocessors -> offer one-time deep-dive + ongoing notice process.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm acceptable liability multiplier range with ELT/legal (1x vs 3x).
- Ask infra: cost delta for single-region true residency vs geo-redundant.
- Get precedent: find last three deals where we conceded export timing and what we charged. (JIRA-LEGAL-383)
- Draft fallback clause for model-output litigation exposure (Asha -> Jordan to draft).

Notes to self:
- Keep counters concise when AE present — show commercial compromise (pricing/insurance) instead of legalese.
- Use 'we can do X if you commit to Y' framing.
- Always push for measurable SLAs (endpoint names + percentiles) instead of fuzzy language.

References: Confluence page with prior redlines: CONFLUENCE-SEC-1452; Sales thread: slack://channel/contract-thread-#legal-negotiations; Deal ticket: JIRA-LEGAL-383.

End of notes.
